selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer matches the advertiser's wellness category and appreciates evidence-backed products. While they typically have low price sensitivity, the advertiser's value proposition of same formulations for half the cost can appeal to their smart system-optimization approach.

The Value-Conscious Shopper directly aligns with the advertiser's competitive edge on price and half-the-cost positioning. Their high price sensitivity and focus on budget-aware purchasing make them an ideal target for budget workout supplements.

The Fitness Enthusiast is a direct fit for the advertiser's core subcategories including pre-workout, creatine, and protein. Their workout frequency and affinity for performance supplements match the advertiser's product line.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent prioritizes subscriptions, whereas the advertiser operates on a one-off business model.
The Gen Z Aesthete focuses on aesthetic-forward packaging and brand values, which conflicts with an advertiser that explicitly competes purely on price rather than marketing.
The Pet Parent focuses entirely on pet health and supplies, which is irrelevant to human workout supplements.
The Affluent Classic has a target age range of 50-68, which falls completely outside the advertiser's target demographic of 18-45.
The Sustainability Buyer focuses on environmental footprint and supply chain transparency, which are not mentioned in the advertiser's price-focused value proposition.
The Convenience-First Millennial relies heavily on subscription services and instant delivery, whereas the advertiser uses a one-off business model.
The Gifter is looking for gift sets and premium presentation for gifting holidays, which does not match a budget-focused, one-off workout supplement brand.
